fields.title: Title
fields.subjects_notification_required: Must the people affected be told?
fields.disposal_method: At the end of the period

breachRisk.unlikely: Unlikely to result in a risk
breachRisk.high_risk: High risk (also tell the people affected)

evaluation_scoring.label: Evaluation or scoring
evaluation_scoring.hint: Profiling or predicting, e.g. credit scoring or performance.

automated_decisions.label: Automated decisions with legal or similar effect
automated_decisions.hint: Decisions made without a person that affect someone significantly.

systematic_monitoring.label: Systematic monitoring
systematic_monitoring.hint: Observing or tracking people, e.g. CCTV or location tracking.

sensitive_data.label: Sensitive or highly personal data
sensitive_data.hint: Health, criminal records, financial data and other special categories.

large_scale.label: Large scale
large_scale.hint: Many people, much data, a long time or a wide area.

matching_datasets.label: Matching or combining datasets
matching_datasets.hint: Joining data from sources in ways people would not expect.

vulnerable_subjects.label: Vulnerable people
vulnerable_subjects.hint: Children, employees, patients or others with less power.

innovative_technology.label: Innovative technology
innovative_technology.hint: New technology or new uses, e.g. biometrics or AI.

prevents_rights.label: Prevents people from using a right or service
prevents_rights.hint: The processing decides access to a service or contract.

form.changeReasonHint: Kept in the revision history so auditors can see why the record changed.
form.personalNotice: This register holds personal data. Record only what you need to handle the matter, and only people with access to requests can see it.
form.awareCorrectionHint: Correcting this moves the 72-hour deadline. The original time stays in the revision history; give the reason below.
form.changeReasonNeeded: Give a reason for correcting the awareness time.
form.notInFuture: This time cannot be in the future.
form.quickIntro: Quick registration: describe what happened and when you became aware of it. The 72-hour clock starts when you save; add the rest afterwards.
form.periodRequired: Give the period in months, or describe it in words.

common.loadFailed: Could not load the data. Try again.

dsr.deadlineExplain: Received {{ received }}. The answer is due within one month, by {{ due }}, unless the deadline is extended.
dsr.extendHint: Only once, before the first deadline, when the request is complex or there are many requests. Tell the requester why within the first month.
dsr.extendMessage: The deadline moves two months later. Explain why; the requester must be told within the first month.
dsr.outcomeMessage: Describe what you did, or why the request was refused. A refusal must tell the person about their right to complain to the authority.
dsr.handlingIntro: Work through the steps in order. Each tick is saved at once and shows in the activity log.

verify_identity.title: Verify who is asking
verify_identity.body: Check the identity before you share or change any data. Ask only for what you need.

search_systems.title: Search the systems
search_systems.body: Find the person's data in every system listed below.

draft_reply.title: Draft the reply
draft_reply.body: Reply in plain language. Choose "Ask AI" at the top of the page for a first draft.

send_reply.title: Send the reply
send_reply.body: Send it before the deadline; the date is noted here.

dsr.noSystems: No active processing activity lists its systems yet.

breach.clockExplain: You became aware on {{ aware }}. The authority must be notified within 72 hours of that moment, unless the breach is unlikely to result in a risk to people.
breach.authorityNotRequired: Decided that no notification is needed.
breach.subjectsNotRequired: Decided that they are not told.
breach.subjectsPending: Must be told, not done yet.

decisionHint.authority: Decide whether the authority must be notified. If not, write down why: the reasoning must be documented even when you do not notify.
decisionHint.subjects: When the risk to people is high they must be told without undue delay, unless an Art. 34(3) exemption applies.

breach.followUpIntro: A personal data breach is also a security incident. Register it as a deviation with corrective action, add the risk it reveals, or give someone a task (ISO 27001 A.5.24–A.5.28, 10.2).

dpia.priorConsultationExplain: The residual risk is still high. Under Art. 36 you must consult the supervisory authority before you start the processing.
dpia.riskDescription: Describe the risk to the people affected

screening.title: Screening
screening.body: Is a DPIA needed? Tick the criteria that apply.

assessment.title: Assessment
assessment.body: Describe the necessity, the risks and the measures.

decision.title: Decision
decision.body: The approver accepts the residual risk or rejects it.

screeningOutcome.required: The screening says a DPIA is required. Start the impact assessment.
screeningOutcome.recommended: One criterion is met: a DPIA is recommended.
screeningOutcome.not_required: No criteria are ticked yet. Tick the ones that apply, or conclude that no DPIA is needed.

dpia.closedNotRequired: Concluded: no DPIA is needed. Keep the screening as documentation.
dpia.notScreenedYet: Not screened yet: tick the criteria that apply.
dpia.authorityList: Datatilsynet also lists processing that always needs a DPIA, for example systematic monitoring of employees, location tracking and large-scale processing of special categories.

lba.liaExplain: Legitimate interests need a documented three-part test: a legitimate purpose, a necessary processing, and a balance that does not override the people's interests and rights.

consent.withdrawHint: When the person withdraws their consent, record it here. Stop the processing that relied on it.
consent.withdrawMessage: The consent is marked as withdrawn now. This cannot be undone; a new consent needs a new record.

decision.title: Decision

notYet.dpia: When the assessment is complete, set the status to "Awaiting decision" so an approver can decide.
notYet.lba: When the assessment is complete, set the status to "Awaiting decision" so an approver can decide.

decision.dialogMessage: Your decision is recorded with your name and the time.

statusHint.ropa: An active record must have the Article 30 information filled in.
statusHint.dpia: Move to "Awaiting decision" when the assessment is complete. A DPIA cannot be marked not required while the screening says it is required.
statusHint.dsr: Completing or refusing a request needs an outcome.
statusHint.breach: A breach is closed only when both notification decisions are on record.
statusHint.processor: A processor can only be active with a signed agreement, or one documented as not required.
statusHint.transfer: A transfer that relies on SCCs, BCRs or another tool can only be active after a positive transfer impact assessment. A transfer under SCCs also needs a linked, signed agreement.
statusHint.retention: Activate the rule once it has been agreed.
statusHint.consent: Consent is active until it is withdrawn.
statusHint.lba: Move to "Awaiting decision" when the assessment is complete.

detail.deleteMessage: The record is removed from the register. It stays in the audit trail.

outputs.title: Documents
outputs.hint: Make this record into a report or letter as Word or PDF. Missing information is shown first.

ai.ropaHint: Describe the processing in your own words. The assistant fills in the form for you to check; nothing is saved until you save.
ai.ropaPlaceholder: For example: we keep customer names, emails and order history in our web shop to deliver orders and handle returns…
ai.applied: The suggestion was added to the form. Review every field before saving.
ai.breachHint: Get a draft risk assessment and a notification recommendation based on this record.
ai.disclaimer: A draft to support you. The decision is yours.
ai.checkRopaHint: The assistant reads the entry and lists what an auditor or the authority would ask for.

ask.field: Explain "{{ field }}" in plain language, in the context of the GDPR.
ask.summarise: Summarise {{ code }} and tell me what is missing or due.
ask.fieldTooltip: Ask the assistant about this field

notices.withdrawn: The withdrawal of {{ code }} was recorded.
notices.executionLogged: The deletion under {{ code }} is logged.

errors.not_found: The record was not found. It may have been deleted.
errors.notFound: The record was not found. It may have been deleted.
errors.forbidden: You do not have access to this.
errors.module_disabled: The privacy module is turned off for this organisation.
errors.invalid_owner: The owner must be a member of the organisation.
errors.invalid_reference: A linked record does not exist: {{ fields }}.
errors.invalid_fields: These fields cannot be changed here: {{ fields }}.
errors.invalid_sort: That sort order is not supported.
errors.invalid_status: This can only be decided while it is awaiting a decision.
errors.ropa_incomplete: Before the record can be active, fill in: {{ fields }}.
errors.dpia_required: The screening shows a DPIA is required, so it cannot be marked as not required.
errors.outcome_required: Record the outcome, or the reason for the refusal, first.
errors.already_extended: The deadline has already been extended once.
errors.extension_too_late: The deadline can only be extended before the first deadline has passed.
errors.delay_reason_required: The authority was notified after 72 hours: give the reason for the delay.
errors.subjects_exemption_required: For a high-risk breach, not telling the people affected needs an Art. 34(3) exemption.
errors.authority_not_required: The decision says the authority need not be notified. Change the decision first.
errors.breach_decisions_pending: Record both notification decisions before closing: {{ fields }}.
errors.dpa_required: A processor can only be active with a signed agreement, or one documented as not required.
errors.dpa_signed_at_required: Enter the date the agreement was signed.
errors.transfer_incomplete: Before the transfer can be active, fill in: {{ fields }}.
errors.tia_incomplete: Complete the transfer impact assessment first.
errors.transfer_not_adequate: The assessment found the protection inadequate, so the transfer cannot be active.
errors.tia_conclusion_required: Enter the conclusion of the transfer impact assessment.
errors.lia_incomplete: Complete the legitimate interests test first: {{ fields }}.
errors.aware_at_forbidden: Only the data protection officer or someone who manages privacy can correct the awareness time.
errors.aware_at_in_future: The awareness time cannot be in the future.
errors.change_reason_required: Give a reason for the change.
errors.scc_contract_required: Link the signed agreement with the standard contractual clauses before the transfer can be active.
errors.scc_contract_unsigned: The linked agreement is not signed and active yet. A transfer under standard contractual clauses can only be active once they are signed.
errors.schedule_not_active: Activate the retention rule before you log deletions.

gaps.intro: Each gap names the article it falls short of. The button opens the fix, already filled in.

lia_missing.title: {{ code }} relies on legitimate interest without an approved assessment
lia_missing.why: Art. {{ article }}: legitimate interest needs a documented three-part test (LIA) before you rely on it.

dpia_missing.title: {{ code }} needs a DPIA ({{ reasons }})
dpia_missing.why: Art. {{ article }}: processing with a high risk needs a data protection impact assessment before it starts.

transfer_missing.title: {{ code }} sends data to {{ countries }} without a recorded transfer
transfer_missing.why: Art. {{ article }}: a transfer out of the EEA needs a transfer tool, such as an adequacy decision or standard contractual clauses.

dpa_missing.title: {{ code }} has no signed data processing agreement ({{ dpaStatus }})
dpa_missing.why: Art. {{ article }}: a processor may only process personal data under a signed agreement.

retention_missing.title: {{ code }} has no retention rule
retention_missing.why: Art. {{ article }}(1)(e): say how long the data is kept and what happens to it afterwards.

ropa_incomplete.title: {{ code }} is missing Art. 30 details: {{ fields }}
ropa_incomplete.why: Art. {{ article }}: the record of processing must hold these details for every activity.

deletion_overdue.title: The deletion under {{ code }} is overdue (due {{ due }})
deletion_overdue.why: Art. {{ article }}(1)(e): log each deletion so you can show that the rule is followed.

supplier_not_processor.title: Supplier {{ code }} processes personal data but is not a registered processor
supplier_not_processor.why: Art. {{ article }}: every supplier that processes personal data for you needs a processor record and an agreement.

retention.title: Set retention rules
retention.body: How long each kind of data is kept, and how it is deleted.

dpia.title: Assess high-risk processing
dpia.body: Screen each activity and carry out a DPIA where one is needed (Art. 35).

requests.title: Agree how you answer requests

breaches.title: Agree how you handle breaches
breaches.body: Who is told, and how you notify the authority within 72 hours.

settings.title: Privacy settings
settings.subtitle: Who is responsible for the processing, and how people reach your data protection officer.

ropa.linkedIntro: Everything that supports this activity: the legal basis, the impact assessment, retention, transfers and consents.
ropa.completenessMissing: Fill these in before you mark the entry as active:
ropa.completenessDone: Every Art. 30 detail is filled in.
ropa.linkedAdd: Not linked yet – create what the processing needs:

retention.activateFirst: Activate the rule to log deletions.
retention.evidencePlaceholder: e.g. a ticket number, a log file or a report
retention.logEmpty: No deletions logged yet. Log each one so you can show that the rule is followed.

explain.eea: {{ country }} is in the EEA: no transfer tool is needed.
explain.adequacy: {{ country }} has an EU adequacy decision: the transfer can rely on it (Art. 45).
explain.adequacy_partial: {{ country }} has an adequacy decision for some recipients only (for example the EU–US Data Privacy Framework). Check that the recipient is covered.
explain.third_country: {{ country }} is a third country: the transfer needs standard contractual clauses or another tool (Art. 46–49) and a transfer impact assessment.
explain.unknown: The country could not be classified.

documents.title: Documents and reports
documents.subtitle: The records Datatilsynet and auditors ask for, made from what you have registered. See what is missing first, then make the document as PDF, Word or Excel.
documents.registersHint: Each register as a spreadsheet or PDF, with the filters you choose.

notices.title: Privacy notices
notices.hint: What you tell customers, employees and job applicants about their personal data (GDPR Art. 13 and 14). Make the notice above, check it, then approve it: it becomes a controlled document that is sent for approval under Documents.
notices.noVersion: No version yet. Make the notice under Documents and reports above.
notices.draft: Draft – a person must check the text
notices.accepted: "{{title}}" is sent for approval under Documents.
notices.sourceChanged: Source data changed – make a new version and approve it as a new revision
notices.builtFrom: Processing activities it is built from ({{n}}):
notices.noActivities: No active processing activity names this group under data subjects yet.

errors.sourceChanged: The data has changed since this version. Make a new version first.
errors.failed: The notice could not be made into a document. Try again.

path.title: Get your privacy in order
path.complete: All four steps are done. Keep the records up to date when something changes.

ropa.title: Map your processing
ropa.body: Write down what personal data you use and why: payroll, customers, newsletter, cameras. This becomes your record of processing.

processors.title: Processors and agreements
processors.body: Suppliers that process personal data for you, and whether the agreement with them (data processing agreement) is signed.

dpia.title: Assess the risk (DPIA)
dpia.body: A risk assessment before you start something new with personal data, such as tracking or health data (data protection impact assessment).

documents.title: Make the documents
documents.body: The record of processing, the privacy notice and the processor list, made from what you have registered.

ropa.purposes: What we use the data for

dpia.residual_risk: Risk left after the measures (residual risk)

transfer.mechanism: What the transfer relies on (transfer mechanism)
transfer.supplementary_measures: Extra measures to protect the data

ropa.draft: Draft – {{ filled }} of {{ total }} facts required by Article 30 are filled in.
ropa.draftComplete: Draft – everything Article 30 requires is filled in. Set the processing to active once it is in use.
ropa.active: Active – the processing is in use and fully described in the record.
ropa.activeIncomplete: Active – but {{ count }} facts required by Article 30 are missing.
ropa.retired: Retired – the processing is no longer in use.

dpia.screening: Screening – step 1 of 3: decide whether a DPIA is needed.
dpia.in_progress: In progress – step 2 of 3: describe the necessity, the risks and the measures.
dpia.awaiting_decision: Awaiting decision – step 3 of 3: the approver accepts the residual risk or rejects it.
dpia.not_required: Not required – the screening shows that no DPIA is needed.
dpia.approved: Approved – {{ name }} accepted the residual risk on {{ date }}.
dpia.rejected: Rejected – {{ name }} rejected the assessment on {{ date }}. The processing cannot start as described.

dsr.open: {{ status }} – the reply is due by {{ date }} ({{ days }} days left).
dsr.overdue: Past the deadline – the reply was due by {{ date }}.
dsr.completed: Completed – the reply was sent on {{ date }}.
dsr.rejected: Refused – the request was refused on {{ date }}.
dsr.withdrawn: Withdrawn – the person withdrew the request.

breach.closed: Closed – the breach is handled and the notification decisions are documented.
breach.notified: Notified – waiting for the breach to be closed.
breach.overdue: Over 72 hours – the deadline to notify the supervisory authority passed on {{ deadline }}.
breach.running: {{ status }} – {{ hours }} hours left to notify the supervisory authority ({{ deadline }}).
breach.decide: {{ status }} – record whether the authority and the people affected must be notified, then close the breach.

transfer.draft: Draft – the transfer to {{ country }} can start once its mechanism is in place and assessed.
transfer.active: Active – data is sent to {{ country }} on the mechanism below.
transfer.suspended: Suspended – no data may be sent to {{ country }} until the transfer is reassessed.
transfer.retired: Retired – the transfer to {{ country }} is no longer in use.

lead.priorConsultation: Prior consultation needed – the residual risk is still high, so the processing must be discussed with the supervisory authority before it starts (Art. 36).
